title: 1963 AHSME Problem 35
statement: The lengths of the sides of a triangle are integers, and its area is also an integer. One side is \(21\) and the perimeter is \(48.\) The shortest side is:

solutions.text:
Let the other sides be \(x\) and \(27-x,\) with \(x\leq27-x.\) The semiperimeter is \(24,\) so Heron’s formula gives \[ \begin{aligned} K^2 &=24\cdot3(24-x)(x-3)\\ &=72(24-x)(x-3). \end{aligned} \] The triangle inequalities give \(4\leq x\leq13.\) Checking these integers, the expression is not a square for \(x=4,\ldots,9,\) while at \(x=10\) it is \(72\cdot14\cdot7=7056=84^2.\) Thus the shortest side is \(10.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Write the other sides as \(x\) and \(27-x\), with semiperimeter \(24\)
Heron’s formula makes the squared area \(72(24-x)(x-3)\)
